home.meta.description: KSP2 Redux is a community-made continuation patch for Kerbal Space Program 2, focused on bug fixes, performance work, and finishing the game.
home.jsonLd.organizationDescription: A community project continuing development of Kerbal Space Program 2, focused on bug fixes, performance, and finishing unimplemented systems.
home.jsonLd.applicationDescription: A community-made continuation patch for Kerbal Space Program 2 that fixes bugs, improves performance, and implements systems left unfinished.
home.hero.intro: KSP2 Redux is a community project focused on fixing Kerbal Space Program 2, improving performance, and finishing systems that were left incomplete.
home.about.heading: What is KSP2 Redux?
home.about.paragraph1: KSP2 Redux is a community-made continuation of Kerbal Space Program 2. The goal is to build out the major systems the game was originally meant to have: colonies, resource management, interstellar travel, multiplayer, and the smaller features those systems depend on.
home.about.paragraph2: That also means doing some foundational work first: fixing bugs, more stable flights, clearer UI, better performance, more complete set of parts, and a stronger base for mods. Redux is not trying to turn KSP2 into a different game or implement every mod feature. The goal is to finish the game as it was originally intended, and make it easier for modders to build on top of that.

home.snapshots.heading: Snapshots most weeks
home.snapshots.paragraph1: Alongside the stable release, Redux puts out snapshots most weeks. They are builds of whatever the team has been working on, released as things get finished instead of being held back for months. Since the first one in August they have added two new moons, mineable uranium, docking port rotation, and a stage recovery system.
home.snapshots.paragraph2: Snapshots are in the beta channel in the Updater, which you can switch to in the settings. The stable channel keeps the tested release, so if you would rather not deal with rough edges, stay there. Snapshots are in heavy development and things will break. When something does, report it with Ctrl+B, or Escape then Report Redux Bug. Every snapshot is written up on the {blogLink}blog{/blogLink} with a full changelog.

faq.meta.title: FAQ | KSP2 Redux
faq.meta.description: Common questions and answers about KSP2 Redux: what it is, how to install it, save compatibility, and where to report problems.
faq.hero.intro: This page covers the usual first questions about Redux: what it is, how installation works, whether saves are usable, and where to report problems.
faq.whatIsRedux.question: What is KSP2 Redux?
faq.whatIsRedux.answer: KSP2 Redux is a fan project built on top of Kerbal Space Program 2. Our goal is to unofficially continue development of the game by fixing bugs, improving performance, and implementing features that were planned for the game but never released, including a full colony system, interstellar travel, and multiplayer.
faq.saves.question: Will my saves work with Redux?
faq.saves.answer: Usually yes, but keep backups. Redux is still changing a lot, so existing saves often work, but no beta project should be treated as risk-free.
faq.performance.question: How much better is the performance?
faq.performance.answer: It depends on the scene and your hardware. Redux has a lot of rendering, simulation, and memory work aimed at reducing stutter and improving framerate, but there is no single number that applies everywhere. We have seen improvements ranging from 30% to 80% higher FPS in normal situations, and even more in some extreme test cases, but it's highly variable.
faq.legal.question: Is Redux legal?
faq.legal.answer: Redux is distributed as binary patches containing only our modifications to the game files. That means that there is no distribution of the original game code, and users must have a legal copy of KSP2 to use Redux.
faq.affiliation.question: Is Redux affiliated with the original KSP2 developers?
faq.affiliation.answer: No. Redux is an independent fan project with no affiliation to the former KSP2 developers, Intercept Games, Private Division, Take-Two Interactive or Fictions. Please do not interpret this project as an official continuation of KSP2's development.
faq.mods.question: Can I use Redux with other mods?
faq.mods.answer1: Most existing mods will need to be updated to work with Redux due to the transition from BepInEx to an integrated mod loader and improvements to the modding API.
faq.mods.answer2: Some asset-only mods, especially simpler part mods, may work with little or no change. More complex code mods usually need some code changes.
faq.install.question: How do I install, update, or uninstall Redux?
faq.install.answer1: Download the latest release of the Updater from {githubLink}GitHub{/githubLink}, run the updater, point it to your KSP2 installation, and select which version of Redux you want to install. The process takes a few minutes depending on your disk speed.
faq.install.answer2: To uninstall Redux, use the uninstall button in the Updater settings. Check our {installationLink}detailed installation guide{/installationLink} for step-by-step instructions.
faq.install.answer3: You can also update between newer beta versions through the Updater. If you are on a version older than beta 5, you will need a fresh install of the latest beta.
faq.features.question: What features are included in Redux?
faq.features.answerCurrent: {strong}Current (Stage 0 - Foundation):{/strong} Performance work, bug fixing, debug tools, heat management, tech tree work, and modding SDK improvements. The {featuresLink}implemented features and fixes{/featuresLink} page has a fuller list.
faq.features.answerPlanned: {strong}Planned:{/strong} Orbital and planetary colonies, a full resource system, supply routes, interstellar work, and multiplayer. The {roadmapLink}roadmap{/roadmapLink} has a full breakdown.
faq.modes.question: What is the difference between Exploration and Frontier mode?
faq.modes.answer: Exploration mode is the lighter progression path where resources mostly work as unlocks. Frontier mode is planned later as a deeper colony economy with production, stockpiles, and supply routes. Read the {guideLink}full Frontier and Exploration guide{/guideLink}.
faq.bugs.question: How do I report bugs?
faq.bugs.answerInGame: Use the in-game bug report feature by pressing {strong}Ctrl+B{/strong} or going to {strong}Escape → Report Redux Bug{/strong}. This automatically attaches screenshots, logs, and save files to help us reproduce the issue.
faq.bugs.answerDiscord: You can also report bugs in the {strong}#🟡redux-bugs{/strong} channel on the {discordLink}KSP2 Redux Discord{/discordLink}.
faq.contribute.question: How can I contribute to the project?
faq.contribute.players: {strong}Players:{/strong} Test beta builds and report bugs
faq.contribute.developers: {strong}Developers:{/strong} Help with code (experience with C#, Unity, or KSP modding preferred)
faq.contribute.translators: {strong}Translators:{/strong} Translate game content into other languages

faq.contribute.guide: The {guideLink}contribution guide{/guideLink} has the current details.

roadmap.meta.title: Roadmap | KSP2 Redux
roadmap.meta.description: See what features KSP2 Redux already has, what we are working on, and what the long-term plans are.
roadmap.hero.intro: Redux is still in the stage where the team is fixing what is broken, smoothing off what is awkward, and putting basic systems in a better state. The point of this page is simply to show what has already been done, what Foundation means, and what is planned after that.
roadmap.panel.title: {label}: {title}
roadmap.progress.label: Roadmap progress
roadmap.changed.heading: What Redux has already changed
roadmap.changed.intro: This is the short version. For a fuller breakdown of features, improvements, and bug fixes already in Redux, read the {featuresLink}implemented features and fixes{/featuresLink} page.
roadmap.opens.heading: Where the roadmap opens up
roadmap.opens.intro: After Foundation, the plan is to move into colonies, then interstellar work, and eventually multiplayer. The exact order may change, but that is the general direction. For a clearer explanation of how the planned resource rules differ, read the {guideLink}Frontier and Exploration modes guide{/guideLink}.
roadmap.help.heading: Help push the roadmap forward
roadmap.help.description: Redux is still a volunteer effort. Testing, bug reports, modding experiments, and asset work all make the next stage easier to reach.
roadmap.milestones.stage-0.label: Stage 0
roadmap.milestones.stage-0.title: Foundation
roadmap.milestones.stage-0.summary: Redux is still in its foundation phase. Right now the work is mostly about making the game more stable, user-friendly, and easier to build on.
roadmap.milestones.stage-0.sections.1.su: This stage includes a lot of rendering, simulation, and memory work that needs to be in a better state before larger systems make sense.
roadmap.milestones.stage-0.sections.2.su: It also means dealing with the bugs that make KSP2 unreliable: flight issues, broken UI behavior, mission logic problems, map view errors, etc.
roadmap.milestones.stage-0.sections.3.ti: Prepare the systems that later stages depend on
roadmap.milestones.stage-0.sections.3.su: Some of the work here directly translates into later stages, including heat, vessel ISRU, tech tree changes, and a more usable modding workflow in the Unity editor.
roadmap.milestones.stage-1-1.label: Stage 1.1
roadmap.milestones.stage-1-1.title: Orbital Colonies
roadmap.milestones.stage-1-1.summary: The first colony step is planned around orbital construction, station infrastructure, and the systems needed to support larger operations off-world.
The goal here is to add orbital colony parts and stations that work as actual construction and support hubs rather than just parked vessels.
In Exploration mode, orbital colonies are meant to connect different locations and handle resource sharing across that network.
This stage also needs clearer power planning once stations start carrying more systems and production equipment.
roadmap.milestones.stage-1-2.label: Stage 1.2
roadmap.milestones.stage-1-2.title: Planetary Colonies
roadmap.milestones.stage-1-2.summary: After the orbital work, the next step is surface colonies: bases on planets and moons, local production, and the management layer that goes with them.
Players should be able to found colonies on planets and moons, then grow them with mining, processing, factories, and launch infrastructure.
This is also where Frontier mode starts to take clearer shape, with more focus on what colonies can actually produce and sustain.
The colony UI needs to cover resources, power, and heat in a way that is understandable without trial and error.
roadmap.milestones.stage-1-3.label: Stage 1.3
roadmap.milestones.stage-1-3.title: Supply Routes and Environment
roadmap.milestones.stage-1-3.summary: Once colonies exist, they still need logistics, environmental constraints, and hardware that fits that scale.
The idea here is to turn flown cargo routes into repeatable supply lines so colonies can support each other without every transfer being manual.
Heat and environment are meant to matter more here, so colony placement is not only a visual choice.
This stage also leaves room for more missions, science content, and heavier hardware suited to moving resources around the Kerbol system.
roadmap.milestones.stage-2.label: Stage 2
roadmap.milestones.stage-2.title: Interstellar
roadmap.milestones.stage-2.summary: After the colony work is in place, the roadmap moves beyond the Kerbol system.
roadmap.milestones.stage-2.sections.1.su: The Debdeb system is planned as the first destination outside Kerbol, with its own worlds, resources, and challenges. More star systems will be added during the rest of the roadmap as well.
roadmap.milestones.stage-2.sections.2.su: That stage also needs hardware to match, so it includes the parts and propulsion systems needed for interstellar travel.
roadmap.milestones.stage-3.label: Stage 3
roadmap.milestones.stage-3.title: Multiplayer
roadmap.milestones.stage-3.summary: The long-term goal is multiplayer, with shared progress and cooperative or competitive play.
roadmap.milestones.stage-3.sections.1.su: The main idea is that multiple players can share one agency and work toward the same goals.
roadmap.milestones.stage-3.sections.2.su: Colonies, logistics, and exploration all change once other people can help with them or interfere with them.
roadmap.features.flight-and-feel.title: Flight and map view reliability
roadmap.features.flight-and-feel.summary: A lot of work has already gone into flight reliability, map view behavior, and the kinds of errors that can ruin an otherwise normal mission.
roadmap.features.flight-and-feel.bullets: Map view and camera behavior have been cleaned up in a lot of frustrating edge cases, including new KSP1-style orbital camera behavior.
SAS stability, time warp behavior, targeting, and vessel state changes have been fixed in several edge cases, along with new vessel categories and icons in the map and tracking station.
Maneuver nodes can now be added and edited while paused, with scroll-wheel precision input for maneuver gizmos.
Flight controls now show notifications when precision input mode changes and when trim is applied or reset.

Docking ports can now be rotated in the 0.2.9 snapshots, struts can be disconnected from the Parts Manager or with action groups, and staging supports stage-based fuel priorities with per-tank flow controls.
A Stage Recovery system, personal waypoints, and a first-person Kerbal camera have been added in the 0.2.9 snapshots.
roadmap.features.ui-and-qol.title: User interface improvements
roadmap.features.ui-and-qol.summary: Some of the most noticeable work is in making the game easier to read and use in the VAB, menus, map view, and Redux-specific UI.
roadmap.features.ui-and-qol.bullets.1: There is now an in-game bug reporter, better search in the part picker, and more consistent UI styling.
roadmap.features.ui-and-qol.bullets.2: Redux has added things like an improved color manager with presets, better orbital info panel, better notifications, and cleaner loading flows.
roadmap.features.ui-and-qol.bullets.3: Various parts of the UI have been improved or completely reworked in the flight view, map view, tracking station, VAB and R&D Center.
roadmap.features.ui-and-qol.bullets.4: We are also gradually working on unifying the UI style and replacing the inconsistent stock UI with our own versions.
roadmap.features.ui-and-qol.bullets.5: The Tracking Station information panel has been rebuilt with resource overlays in the 0.2.9 snapshots, and the launch countdown has been updated.
roadmap.features.content-and-presentatio: While Foundation is all about building a stronger base for the game, there is also plenty of new content:
New radiators, SM+ engines, fuel tanks, adapters, decouplers, separators, boosters, command pods, probe cores, cameras, and decals have been added to the game.
The tech tree and missions have been expanded, including new gateway missions and tech tree nodes for new parts.
Visual and EVA additions include better clouds, sun flares, planet-specific reentry colors, helmet lights, EVA parachutes, and supersampling for flight and the VAB.
Campaign-related additions include custom flags, a statistics window, and clearer vessel categories and icons in the map and tracking station.
Two new celestial bodies, Drast and Beyl, both moons of Dres, have been added in the 0.2.9 snapshots, built with the new in-engine planet authoring tools.

Mineable uranium has been added to Duna and Pol in the 0.2.9 snapshots, scannable from orbit, extractable with drills and stored in solid resource containers, alongside further SM+ parts and new missions.
roadmap.features.modding-and-ecosystem.s: A big part of the project is making it easier to create and maintain mods for the game.
roadmap.features.modding-and-ecosystem.b: We have upgraded the game's Unity engine version from 2022.3 to 6.4+ and our Redux SDK lets modders make full use of Unity's features.
Project Shakespeare is an experimental KSP1 part mod loader, which serves as a preview for our future comprehensive editor tooling for helping KSP1 modders port their parts to KSP2 Redux.
The SDK includes improved part modding tools, including part icons, drag cubes and reentry meshes generation, tools for making engine plumes, fairing shrouds, reusable audio components, and more
Patch Manager now uses Lua scripting with better diagnostics, dedicated VS Code extension, generated stubs, patch ordering controls, and a new config system.
Our crossplatform Updater app reduces the amount of setup and maintenance work around the game.
